statement: A club has $50$ members. Of these, $28$ own a bicycle, $19$ own a skateboard, and $9$ own neither. How many members own a bicycle but not a skateboard?

choices.misconception: I found the number who own both, 28 + 19 - 41 = 6, and stopped there instead of finding bicycle-only owners.
I subtracted the skateboard owners from the bicycle owners, 28 - 19 = 9, but skateboard owners are not all bicycle owners.
I found the number who own a skateboard but not a bicycle, 19 - 6 = 13, which is the other one-item group.
I subtracted the 9 members who own neither from the bicycle owners, 28 - 9 = 19, but those 9 are not counted in the 28.

hints: How many members own at least one of the two items?
$50 - 9 = 41$ members own at least one. Use $28 + 19$ compared with $41$ to find how many own both.

solutions.reliable: Since $9$ members own neither, $50 - 9 = 41$ own at least one item. Adding $28 + 19 = 47$ counts the owners of both items twice, so $47 - 41 = 6$ own both. Then $28 - 6 = 22$ own a bicycle but not a skateboard.
solutions.elegant: Everyone who does not own a skateboard is either a bicycle-only owner or owns neither. That is $50 - 19 = 31$ members, so bicycle-only owners number $31 - 9 = 22$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
